title: Discovering non-linear dynamics of miRNAs in Alzheimer's disease-related cognitive impairment: a cross-species approach with explainable machine learning.
summary: Cross-species human serum and Alzheimer mouse hippocampal miRNA expression datasets were analyzed with mRMR selection and nonlinear SVM-RBF and kNN classifiers compared against linear classifiers, with SHAP interpretation. The nonlinear models outperformed the linear ones; mild cognitive impairment versus controls reached AUC 0.844; miR-155-5p was a stable primary driver while miR-339-5p and miR-455-5p were context-dependent; mouse expression changes are reported. The relations are retrospective, observational and model-derived, with cross-species and correlational limits, and no causal mechanism or prospective screening performance is established.
